subject: Ledgerly post-call: integration pattern recommendations & SDK demo
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@ledgerly.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@ledgerly.io>
Date: 2029-05-16T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery — Ledgerly / Redwood integration (today)

Thanks for the call today — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and asks so we can scope POC: 

- Goal: build an intelligent reconciliation helper in Ledgerly that suggests likely matches for transactions and surfaces a ranked set of matches for the end user (UI).
- Volume: roughly 250k reconciliations/month, median sequence lengths ~300 tokens, peak concurrent users ~40.
- Non-functional: must not persist PII, needs region-local processing (US), 99.9% availability target for the feature.

As discussed, we want guidance from Redwood on: 
1) SDK onboarding + example call patterns (server-side vs edge).
2) Auth model that works with our multi-tenant app (we prefer short-lived tokens from our backend).
3) Structured outputs: we need a deterministic JSON schema for candidates + confidence scores and an optional reranker stage.
4) Tool/function calling: recommended approach for defining tools (search, DB-proxy, enrichment) and how to handle parallel tool invocations + graceful degradation when a tool times out.

Can you send a short mutual action plan + some sample tool-defs we can adapt? Also curious if the reranker should run as a separate embedding-based step or inside the model prompt (we heard pros/cons on cost and latency).

Cheers,
Samir
CTO, Ledgerly

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledgerly.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery — Ledgerly / Redwood integration (today)

Samir — thanks for the clear recap. Great meeting. Attached: a lightweight tool-definition template (redwood-tool-def-template.xlsx) and a first-pass integration architecture diagram (ledgerly-integration-arch-v1.png). High-level answers below plus proposed next steps.

Top-line guidance (TL;DR):
- SDK onboarding: use our server-side Python/Node SDK for the candidate generation call (single request per reconciliation event). We recommend batching at 200ms window for throughput if you expect bursts.
- Auth: short-lived JWTs issued by your backend to Redwood API keys (mutual TLS optional for Dedicated/Private). We'll share a token-exchange pattern that maps to your tenant IDs.
- Structured output: define a strict JSON schema (we provided a sample in the template) and use Redwood's structured output validation + schema enforcement for deterministic parsing.
- Reranker: for 250k/mo, the common pattern is candidate generation (model A) -> embeddings + ANN reranker (vector DB) -> final model re-score for UI. This gives the best cost/latency balance.
- Tool calling: define tools as idempotent microservices (search, enrichment, ledger-proxy). Use parallel calls with circuit-breaker timeouts and fallback to cached results. See Sean's note below for specifics.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
1) We share example tool-defs and SDK snippets (today) — attached.
2) Technical workshop: 1.5hr with Sean + infra (Wed 5/22 10am PT) to validate auth/routing and run a sample call.
3) POC: 4-week bench + integration with vector DB; success metrics: 90% top-3 accuracy and median latency <350ms.

Would Wed 5/22 10am PT work for the technical workshop? Once you confirm, I'll book and include the agenda.

Best,

Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com]
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledgerly.io>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-16T19:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery — Ledgerly / Redwood integration (today)

Samir — adding a few pragmatic patterns from infra/serving that we use a lot for this exact workflow: 

1) Tool definitions (recommended minimal fields): id, name, description, input_schema, output_schema, timeout_ms, retry_policy, confidence_field. Keep inputs small (IDs + short context) and avoid sending PII. Example row from template: 
   - id: search_tx
   - name: transaction_candidate_search
   - input_schema: {"account_id":"string","query_text":"string","limit":"integer"}
   - output_schema: {"candidates":[{"id":"string","score":"number","metadata":"object"}]}

2) Parallel tools: fan out calls to search_tx and enrichment_service concurrently. Use an aggregator that waits up to 200ms for tool responses then proceeds with available candidates. Important: make all downstream steps idempotent.

3) Error handling and graceful degradation: 
   - Circuit breakers per tool (5xx or latency spike trips CB for 60s).
   - Timeouts: client-level 500ms, tool-level 200ms default. If a tool times out, return partials and mark candidate source = "fallback_cache".
   - Retries: only for transient 502/503, exponential backoff, max 2 retries. Do not retry on 4xx from tool.

4) Reranker patterns: 
   - Option A (latency-savvy): generate candidates -> compute embeddings for each candidate (server-side), query ANN store (Faiss/Redis) -> pass top-N to small re-ranker model for final scoring.
   - Option B (cost-savvy): have the base model include a compact similarity scoring in prompt and only run re-ranker for ambiguous cases.

5) Structured output enforcement: include a JSON schema in the prompt and validate with Redwood's schema-enforcement API before consuming results. Fail-open policy: if schema validation fails, surface raw output flagged for manual review; do not auto-apply.

6) SDK/auth specifics: 
   - Use our Node SDK's with built-in request batching and KV cache helper.
   - For multi-tenant mapping: issue short-lived session tokens from your backend that include tenant hash; Redwood verifies the token and tags usage.

I put code snippets in sdk-quickstart-snippets.txt attached (examples for parallel Promise.all patterns, timeout wrappers, and sample tool-def JSON). Happy to run through them in the workshop.

—Sean
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@ledgerly.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@ledgerly.io>
Date: 2029-05-17T02:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery — Ledgerly / Redwood integration (today)

Thanks — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our infra team: 

- SLA/latency: can you confirm Redwood's hosted SLA regarding median P95 token latency for generation and for an end-to-end candidate + rerank flow? We need numbers to compare against our 350ms goal for median.
- Reranker placement: we lean toward Option A (embeddings + ANN then re-score) but want a sense of cost delta (approx tokens + embedding calls). Can you send a ballpark cost comparison for 250k recs/mo with top-20 candidate embedding then top-5 re-score?
- Data residency: we will likely want regional routing (US only) with no replication to EU. How do we configure that in Dedicated vs Hosted?

Also, procurement timeline: we are aiming for an internal vendor review week of 6/3 and would need a short commercial proposal by 5/28 to hit that. Is that feasible?

Samir

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@ledgerly.io>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2029-05-17T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Discovery — Ledgerly / Redwood integration (today)

Samir — great questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- SLA/latency: Hosted API median P95 generation depends on model family; for the model families we discussed we typically see P95 token latency in the 40–120ms range for single-token generations. For an end-to-end flow (candidate gen + embeddings + re-rank) our guideline is median <350ms in US regions under expected load with Dedicated sizing; Hosted can hit that in many cases but we recommend Dedicated for strict SLOs. I'll include a short benchmark table in the proposal.
- Cost estimate: we'll produce a ballpark for the two patterns (Option A vs Option B) — expect Option A to be 25–40% higher in unit cost due to embedding/store ops but better accuracy. We'll send a 1-page cost sketch by 5/24 and the commercial proposal by 5/28.
- Data residency: Hosted supports region pinning for most customers; Dedicated gives stronger guarantees and private control plane options (no cross-region replication). We'll enumerate the configurations in the proposal so procurement can review.

ACTION ITEMS: 
- Redwood: cost sketch (5/24), commercial proposal & benchmark table (5/28), technical workshop booking (once you confirm 5/22) — Jasmine to schedule.
- Ledgerly: confirm 5/22 technical workshop or propose alternate times; share any security questionnaire in advance.

I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 5/22 10am PT and include Sean + infra. Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Jasmine
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
